audit.why: Left as TRICKY/7 because I could not verify Wukong's kit — the brief's enemyKit is null. The content prose reads as a Lillia-favoured lane from 2 onward and the win rate is 57.14%, but I will not move the difficulty enum on prose alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the chart disagreed with its own why: Lillia was given Level 1 and Level 6 (which the whys call a wash and a coin-flip) while Wukong was given Levels 3, 4-5, first item and 2+ items (which the whys call Lillia's peak and takeover).
audit.why: whys[3] 'Levels 4-5 are your peak lane window'; whys[5] his armour is 'wasted stats' against magic burn; whys[6] 'At 2+ items you win every extended kite fight'; whys[0] and whys[4] describe a wash and a coin-flip. Packet levelChart reads Skill, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Skill, Lillia, Lillia — an exact match to the prose.
audit.corrected: All seven rows aligned to the prose in both layers with matching ratings, proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names only Nimbus Strike and never mentions the Warrior Trickster clone, which is the one interaction that can waste Lillia's 110-150s ultimate.
audit.why: The content layer already establishes it (whys[4], spikes[1], wants.foe[1]): the clone can absorb the Lilting Lullaby sleep instead of his real body. That belongs on the full layer's key-interaction and don't lines, where a player actually reads it before the fight. Lillia's side of the maths is verifiable: R is 150/130/110s and requires Dream Dust already applied, so a sleep spent on a decoy costs two minutes.
audit.corrected: Clone-baits-your-R now stated in report[5], dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[0].d.

edits.before: Q's outer ring on his last-hits plus the passive speed means he literally cannot touch you at level 1.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — one ability each and no kite chain, so farm at range and set the lane up.

edits.before: Lilting Lullaby online — your jungler's ganks are now guaranteed, and any overstep becomes a sleep-execute.
edits.after: Lilting Lullaby is online, but Warrior Trickster's clone can eat the sleep — 6 is a genuine coin-flip.

edits.before: Track Wukong’s Nimbus Strike: His only gap-close — he cannot reach you while it is down. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Nimbus Strike is his only gap-close — while it is down he cannot reach you. Warrior Trickster's clone can also eat your R sleep.

edits.before: Wukong spends Nimbus Strike early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Warrior Trickster leaves a clone behind — sleep his real body, never the decoy.

edits.before: That’s Wukong’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His W clone can eat your R — check which body you are on before committing.

notes: The brief's enemyKit is NULL for Wukong, so no cooldown, range or flag on his side could be verified. I added no numeric claim about his abilities and restated the clone interaction only because the content layer already asserts it. If a Wukong kit file exists, this matchup deserves a second pass to add Crushing Blow's armour shred and Nimbus Strike's real cooldown. Voice defect: content early/mid/late are written in first person ('I only have Blooming Blows', 'my best lane window'), unlike the rest of the champion's pages.
